title: Content view selection: priority vote in registry, raw fallback
answers: How do content views pick a renderer?
What happens when a contentview fails to prettify?
How is content_type metadata built for views?
body:
1. Input prep: `mitmproxy/contentviews/_utils.py:get_data` → (content, enc), falls back to raw_content if decode fails; `_utils.py:make_metadata` builds `Metadata` with normalised `content_type` (type/subtype via `http.parse_content_type`).
2. Selection: `mitmproxy/contentviews/_registry.py:ContentviewRegistry.get_view` — named view wins (unknown name → warning, auto); auto calls `render_priority(data, metadata)` on every registered view, picks highest; views that raise are logged and skipped.
3. Protocol: `_api.py:Contentview.render_priority` returns float, <0 = can't handle, default 0.
4. Render: `contentviews/__init__.py:prettify_message` calls `view.prettify`; in auto mode on exception falls back to `_view_raw.py` raw view with `[failed to parse as X]`; explicit view shows the error. Output passes through `strutils.escape_control_characters`.
Examples: `_view_json.py:JSONContentview.render_priority` 1 for json types (0 on empty); `_view_image/view.py:ImageContentview` 1 for image/* except +xml; `_view_xml_html.py:XmlHtmlContentview` 1 for known types, 0.4 if `strutils.is_xml(data)`; `_view_raw.py:RawContentview` always 0.1 (wins only if all others <=0).
